Hi, I am a new user trying to train myself with Lean:
I've tried formalizing the theorem finrank_weightSpace_eq_one_of_isIrreducible for the lie algebra

sl2(K)sl_2(\mathbb{K})sl2​(K)

and its proof.
The draft PR is here.
Feel free to leave your comments.
Thanks in advance

Hi, welcome! Thanks for following the guideline and disclosing the AI usage. A common phenomenon among AI-assisted code is what I call "have-Hadouken" (from this): it often contains code like

have lemma1 : ... := by
  have slight_variation_of_lemma1 : ... := by
    have yet_another_slight_variation : ... := by
      ..

Most of time this can be "folded" into prettier proof, by

  1. move all nested haves out
  2. combine haves that are similar by chaining tactics
  3. invert the proof order to eliminate have blocks
  4. separate out useful lemma as its own theorem/lemma
btw, you can type #37010 here and the bot will also react to it and PR status as emote

Thank you.
I personally have introduced this  "have-Hadouken" structure in several proofs to gain a better view of the state. But I will try removing them later.
But concerning the part generated by AI that exceeds my level, should I replace them with a sorry or it's ok with the comments indicating the usage ?

Here is a few things I learned from contributing to mathlib

  • It won't merge anything with sorry. sorry temporarily appearing in a draft PR for further comments is fine, but reviewers don't have infinite time to help with filling every sorry
  • Adding comment about AI usage is probably ok, but it doesn't lower the standard reviewers use to review the code.

And this part of the guideline is crucial

It is essential that you can vouch for all the code submitted in a PR, and understand all the content written by an AI. If you don't, then it is possible that the PR actually has negative value to the community, and you are expecting others to do the real work for you!

I see.
I basically followed the typical procedure that we see in textbook. The code is understandable but more questions may be needed to test if I have missed something important.
Anyway I will check out the guideline and improve the structure first.

Thanks for the updates. I should clarify that I know little about Lie algebra, so I can't provide advice on the math part.

About this

I only managed to formalize the finite-dimensional version, although the theorem also holds in the infinite-dimensional case.

What is the gap in the proof between the finite version and the infinite version, and what work needs to be done to close the gap? (again, I am not qualified to judge to the answer, but I assume other people are interested in learning the obstacle you are facing)

At this point, I only have the prerequisites (linear algebra and basics of lie algebra and representation) for the finite version, so I haven't looked deeper into the formalization of the infinite case, where the existence of a primitive vector is not guaranteed. That's about all I can see for now. A quick search suggests that we might need heavy tools like Casimir operators and the universal enveloping algebra, which are totally beyond my current level.

I think the general statement you want is: if an irreducible representation over a field has an h-eigenvector, then all h-eigenvalues have multiplicity one. I don’t think you need heavy tools for this.

Thanks, that's a great idea and I'm working on it now.
Btw, should I break down the current PR? I've shortened the code as much as possible, but the finite case is already 350 lines. I'm worried that adding the infinite case will make it too daunting to review. On the other hand, keeping the PR self-contained seems to facilitate the review of the whole process. What do you think?
